comparison: Both evaluate baseline antibody measurements (C20, C21, C24). OpenEval finds the serological data well-supported with appropriate statistical tests. Peer reviewers accepted these baseline characterizations without challenge, noting the study was 'carefully done' and 'well-designed.' Strong agreement on this foundational data.

Both address the stimulation protocol (C25, C26). OpenEval finds the short stimulation time appropriate and validated by data in Figures 2b-c. However, Peer Reviewer 2 fundamentally questions whether antigen-specific responses were actually detected, stating 'I am not convinced that the in vitro antigen stimulation assay worked as intended.' Major disagreement on validity of core methodology.

Both address methodological aspects (C49, C53, C54, C59). OpenEval supports the exclusion criteria and use of multiple markers for cTFH identification. Peer reviewers acknowledged methodological strengths including 'cutting-edge spectral flow cytometry' and 'excellent data analysis.' Agreement on technical approach quality, though peer reviewers questioned its application to antigen-specific detection.

Both evaluate age-dependent differences in cTFH distribution (C27, C28). OpenEval finds these well-supported by EdgeR analysis with appropriate FDR corrections. Peer reviewers acknowledged 'excellent data analysis' but Reviewer 2 questioned whether these represent true antigen-specific responses versus 'overall CD4 T cell compartment plus or minus antigenic stimulation.' Partial disagreement on interpretation.

Both address C29 regarding antigen-specific differences. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to FDR of 0.08 exceeding conventional threshold, noting need for validation. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer 2 fundamentally questioning whether antigen-specific responses were detected at all. Agreement on uncertainty, but for different reasons.

Both evaluate IL-4 and IFN-γ/IL-21 responses (C30, C31). OpenEval finds the predominant IL-4 response well-supported and biologically plausible. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 expressing 'serious concerns about cytokine detection' and questioning whether IL-4 staining represents 'autofluorescence rather than true cytokine signals.' Strong disagreement on data validity.

Both address differential transcription factor induction (C32, C33, C34). OpenEval finds these supported by paired statistical comparisons. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY: while Reviewer 3 noted ICOS and Bcl6 expression 'strengthens the case,' Reviewer 2's concern that 'no antigen-specific CXCR5+ CD4 T cells could be analysed' undermines confidence. Disagreement on whether responses are antigen-specific.

Both evaluate adult-specific response patterns (C35, C36, C37, C38). OpenEval finds the restricted response pattern in adults well-supported. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, citing the same fundamental concerns about cytokine detection validity and antigen-specificity that apply throughout. Disagreement on data interpretation.

Both address associations between cTFH subsets and antibody levels (C39, C40). OpenEval finds these supported with appropriate FDR corrections. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether associations represent 'true antigen-specific memory responses or simply reflect overall T cell compartment differences.' Disagreement on whether correlations are meaningful.

Both evaluate the key finding about age-dependent cTFH engagement (C41, C42). OpenEval finds this well-supported by cumulative data as a major finding. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer 2 directly challenging that the study 'is not really on antigen-specific T cells' and the editor noting 'analysis and interpretation of antigen-specific CD4 cTfh responses remain incomplete.' Major disagreement on core conclusions.

Both address vaccine efficacy implications (C44, C47). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation requires longitudinal studies with clinical outcomes. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer 4 noting functional significance 'requires functional and transfer experiments in animal models.' Agreement that vaccine recommendations are speculative, compounded by peer concerns about underlying data validity.

Both address study design elements (C48, C50, C51, C58, C60 for OpenEval; C49-C54, C59 for peer). OpenEval finds the cross-sectional design clearly stated and appropriate. Peer reviewers acknowledged the study was 'well-designed' with methodological strengths. Agreement on study design quality.

OpenEval evaluates MC04 association with HRP2 antibody levels (C56, C57) as SUPPORTED with some speculation about short-term production. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates background context on malaria vaccines (C1-C9) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge background claims.
OpenEval evaluates TFH biology background (C10-C15, C46) as SUPPORTED with foundational literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge established TFH biology.
OpenEval evaluates prior literature on cTFH responses to malaria (C16-C19) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge literature summaries.
OpenEval evaluates rationale for studying cellular responses beyond antibodies (C45) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge this rationale.
